gn.title: Creation, fall and the patriarchs
gn.summary: In Egypt and Mesopotamia, the world began with many gods and the pharaoh at the center. Israel, fresh from slavery, needed to know where it came from. Genesis opens the Bible with one Creator, the fall, the flood, and Abraham—the family through which God promises to bless the nations.
gn.author: Tradition: Moses

ex.title: Liberation and alliance at Sinai
ex.summary: Egypt was the superpower of the time; Israel, labor. The book narrates the plagues, Easter, the sea and Mount Sinai, where a slave people receives the Law. Behind is the Nile empire; Ahead, the desert and the promised land.
ex.author: Tradition: Moses

lv.title: The cult of a holy people
lv.summary: Camped in the desert, among nations with temples and idols, Israel receives the map of worship: sacrifices, festivals, priests and purity. Leviticus teaches how a people approaches a holy God without copying neighboring sanctuaries.
lv.author: Tradition: Moses

nm.title: The march in the desert
nm.summary: From Sinai to the edge of Canaan, the people are counted, murmur and almost lose their inheritance. Forty years in the desert separate two generations. Numbers is the diary of a nation in transit, between the Egypt that remained and the land that is not yet theirs.
nm.author: Tradition: Moses

dt.title: The testament of Moses
dt.summary: At the gates of Canaan, the generation that did not see Egypt hears the Law again. Moses summarizes the covenant before he died: loving the Lord, not forgetting, choosing life. All around, the people and gods of the land that are about to enter.
dt.author: Tradition: Moses

js.title: The conquest of the land
js.summary: Moses died. Joshua crosses the Jordan and the city-states of Canaan fall one by one. The book shows the land as a gift — and warns that the inheritance only remains if the people remain faithful.
js.author: Tradition: Joshua

jz.title: When everyone did what they wanted
jz.summary: Without a king and without Moses, the tribes forget the Lord, suffer at the hands of neighboring peoples and cry out for deliverance. A judge rises, peace is short-lived, the cycle begins again. Judges portrays Israel at large—and the emptiness of that freedom.
jz.author: Tradition: Samuel

rt.title: Fidelity in the time of judges
rt.summary: While Judges shows the chaos, Ruth tells of a family in Bethlehem and a Moabite who clings to Israel. Basically, David's line begins in a barley field — a small grace in a difficult time.
rt.author: Unknown

1sm.title: Samuel, Saul and the request for a king
1sm.summary: The Philistines dominate the coast; the tribes want a king “like the nations”. Samuel anoints Saul. The book asks what happens when the throne replaces obedience — and prepares David's ascension.
1sm.author: Tradition: Samuel and prophets

2sm.title: David's reign
2sm.summary: David unifies the tribes, takes Jerusalem and receives the promise of an eternal home. Then it falls, and the book doesn't hide it. The height of Israel and the crack of the king occupy the same stage.
2sm.author: Tradition: court prophets

1rs.title: Solomon, the temple and the divided kingdom
1rs.summary: Solomon asks for wisdom and builds the temple; the heart then goes astray and the kingdom breaks apart. Egypt, Syria and Assyria prowl. 1 Kings reads Israel's policy by covenant—not by palace size.
1rs.author: Tradition: prophets
1rs.audience: The people in or after exile

2rs.title: The fall of Samaria and Jerusalem
2rs.summary: The North falls to Assyria; Judah resists until Babylon burns the city and the temple. Prophets warned. 2 Kings was written in the shadow of exile: the question is not who had the most army, but what the infidelity cost.
2rs.author: Tradition: prophets

1cr.title: Names, worship and the memory of David
1cr.summary: After exile, under the Persian empire, the people need to recognize themselves again. Chronicles begins again with genealogies, the temple and David. It's not just repeating Samuel and Reis: it's giving identity back to those who returned.
1cr.author: Tradition: Ezra

2cr.title: Judah, the temple and revivals
2cr.summary: From Solomon to captivity, the focus is Judah and the cult. Wicked kings and reforms alternate. For the community that rebuilt the temple, the lesson is clear: standing walls are not enough if the heart does not return.
2cr.author: Tradition: Ezra

ed.title: The return and the Law again
ed.summary: Cyrus of Persia overthrows Babylon and sends the Jews home. Ezra reintroduces the Law; the second temple rises. A small people begins again under an empire — without a king from the house of David, but with the Scriptures.
ed.author: Ezra

ne.title: Walls and reform in Jerusalem
ne.summary: Nehemiah leaves the Persian palace to build the walls in 52 days, under threat from his neighbors. Then read the Law in public. Restoration here is stone and repentance — city and people at the same time.
ne.author: Nehemiah

et.title: Jews in the palace of Persia
et.summary: In the diaspora, far from the temple, a decree threatens to extinguish the people. Esther risks Xerxes' throne. God is not named in the book—but providence turns every scene in the heart of the empire.
et.author: Unknown

jo.title: The suffering of the righteous
jo.summary: The scene is the age of the patriarchs, in the East. Job loses everything without any guilt to explain it. Friends recite formulas; God responds from the whirlwind. The book enters into the ancient wisdom debate: why do the innocent suffer?
jo.author: Unknown

sl.title: Israel's hymnal
sl.summary: Prayers of David and others, composed over centuries—from Solomon's temple to exile and back. Lament, praise, king and pilgrim. Psalms are the voice of Israel before God, at a party and in a dark night.
sl.author: David et al.

pv.title: Wisdom for everyday life
pv.summary: In the court of Israel and in dialogue with the wisdom of the East, wise men bring together sentences about language, work, justice and family. The center is one: the fear of the Lord. Without it, cleverness becomes ruin.
pv.author: Tradition: Solomon and wise men

ec.title: Everything is vapor
ec.summary: A wise man — tradition says Solomon — tests pleasure, work and knowledge at the height of prosperity. Everything is vapor. Ecclesiastes is not cynicism: it is a warning not to idolize the sun, and an invitation to fear God on the ground of life.
ec.author: Tradition: Solomon

ct.title: Song of love and alliance
ct.summary: Bridal poetry from the ancient East, attributed to Solomon. Two lovers seek each other in bold and pure language. Tradition also reads here God's love for his people — the human and the holy in the same song.
ct.author: Tradition: Solomon

is.title: The Holy One of Israel and the Servant
is.summary: While Assyria swallows nations, Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple of Jerusalem. He announces judgment on Judah and, in the same breath, a boy, a suffering Servant and new heavens. Prophecy of imperial crisis — and of hope greater than the empire.
is.author: Isaiah

jr.title: The prophet of the fall of Jerusalem
jr.summary: For decades, Jeremiah preaches repentance as Babylon approaches. Almost no one listens. The city falls in 586 BC. In the midst of the ruin, God promises a new covenant written in the heart.
jr.author: Jeremiah

lm.title: Jerusalem's mourning
lm.summary: After the fire, five crying poems. The burned city, the temple on the ground, the people on their way to exile. Lamentations gives language to pain—and yet affirms that the Lord's mercies are new every morning.
lm.author: Tradition: Jeremiah

ez.title: The Glory of God in Exile
ez.summary: A priest taken to Babylon, Ezekiel sees the glory leaving the temple — and promises that he will return. God was not confined to the ruins of Jerusalem: he reached the exiles along the canals and spoke of a new heart and a new temple.
ez.author: Ezekiel

dn.title: Faithful in the palace of empires
dn.summary: Young Jew at the court of Babylon, after Persia. Daniel serves kings without bending the knee. Visions show empires that rise and fall. The thesis of the book: the Most High rules the kingdom of men.
dn.author: Daniel

os.title: God's love for an unfaithful people
os.summary: In the northern kingdom, rich and idolatrous, on the eve of Assyria, Hosea marries Gomer to stage the betrayed alliance. God doesn't give up. The book is holy jealousy — and a love that buys back those who ran away.
os.author: Hosea

jl.title: Locusts and the Day of the Lord
jl.summary: A plague devastates the countryside of Judah. ​​Joel reads the disaster as a call to fast and announces the day of the Lord. It promises the Spirit poured out on all flesh — a text the church will hear again in Acts 2.
jl.author: Joel

am.title: Justice in the time of plenty
am.summary: Israel lives in apparent peace and oppresses the poor. A cattle driver from Judah confronts the North: crowded parties, empty worship. Amos announces that the Lord's day is not a celebration for those who crush others. Assyria has not yet arrived — but the sentence is already at the door.
am.author: Amos

ob.title: Edom's pride
ob.summary: When Jerusalem falls, Edom — Israel's brother — mocks and takes advantage. Obadiah, the least of the prophets, says that the pride of the mountain does not escape. A short oracle against those who applaud other people's misfortunes.
ob.author: Obadiah

jn.title: The prophet who flees from Nineveh
jn.summary: Nineveh is the capital of Assyria, the terror of the century. Jonah prefers the sea to preaching to enemies. God insists. The point of the book is not the fish: it is a prophet angry because the Lord forgives too much.
jn.author: Jonas

mq.title: Justice, mercy and a king in Bethlehem
mq.summary: Assyria on the border, corrupt leaders at home. Micah denounces venal princes and prophets — and points to Bethlehem as the birthplace of the eternal ruler. Judgment and hope in the same breath.
mq.author: Micah

na.title: The fall of Nineveh
na.summary: Decades after Jonah, Assyria does not repent. Naum announces the collapse of the capital that oppressed the world. Consolation for Judah: no empire is eternal before God.
na.author: Nahum

hc.title: Until when, Lord?
hc.summary: Injustice grows in Judah; Babylon rises on the horizon. Habakkuk asks why evil wins. God responds with a frightening plan — and with the phrase: the just will live by faith. The prophet ends up singing, without having understood everything.
hc.author: Habakkuk

sf.title: The day of the Lord and a rest that sings
sf.summary: Idols in Jerusalem, nations around. Zephaniah sees a day of darkness — and, in the end, God singing for a humble people. Judgment is not the last word. God's joy is.
sf.author: Zephaniah

ag.title: Rebuild the temple
ag.summary: Eighteen years after the return from Persia, the temple is still a ruin and the people's houses are already boarded up. Haggai confronts the community and the work begins again in 520 BC. Priority: God's house, not just ours.
ag.author: Haggai

zc.title: Visions of Restoration and the King to Come
zc.summary: A colleague of Haggai, Zechariah animates the reconstruction with visions — candelabra, horses, a King on a donkey. The temple is now; the horizon is bigger. God is not finished with Jerusalem yet.
zc.author: Zechariah

ml.title: The last prophet of the Old Testament
ml.summary: The temple is standing, love has cooled. Malachi demands sincere worship, marriage and tithing — and promises a messenger who prepares the way. Then, four centuries of silence until John the Baptist.
ml.author: Malachi

mt.title: Jesus, the Messiah of Israel
mt.summary: Judea under Rome, messianic wait in the air. Matthew writes for those who knew the Law: Jesus is the son of David, the new Moses, the King of the Sermon on the Mount. Each page links the Nazarene to the Scriptures Israel already had.
mt.author: Matthew

mc.title: The Gospel on the move
mc.summary: Probably the oldest of the four, written with the church of Rome in view—and perhaps under persecution. Mark is short and quick: Jesus acts with power and walks to the cross. A Lord who suffers with his disciples.
mc.author: Frames

lc.title: Jesus for all people
lc.summary: Luke, a Greek doctor, orders the report for Theophilus and the Roman world. Women, the poor, Samaritans and the lost occupy the center. The Gospel does not stay in Israel: it is born in Bethlehem and points to the nations.
lc.author: Lucas

joao.title: The Word became flesh
joao.summary: At the end of the first century, with debates about who Jesus is, John chooses signs and dialogues instead of repeating others. The purpose is written: to believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and to have life in his name.
joao.author: John the apostle

at.title: The church and the Gospel until Rome
at.summary: Continuation of Luke. From Jerusalem to Rome, the Spirit pushes witnesses through synagogues, Greek cities, and courtrooms across the empire. Acts is the map of a faith that did not remain in the upper room.
at.author: Lucas

rm.title: The Gospel of God's righteousness
rm.summary: Paul had not yet been to Rome, the capital of the world, when he wrote his most dense letter. Jews and Gentiles in the same church, tensions in the air. All have sinned; Christ justifies; the Spirit dwells. The charter that formed the church.
rm.author: Paul

1co.title: A gifted and divided church
1co.summary: Corinth is Puerto Rico, worship of many gods, loose morals. The church imitates the city: parties, immorality, disorderly supper. Paul calls back to the cross. Gifts without love do not build; resurrection is not optional.
1co.author: Paul

2co.title: Wounded ministry, power in weakness
2co.summary: The relationship cracked. False apostles sell prestige. Paul defends the apostolate without boasting: treasure in an earthen vessel. His most personal letter is born out of conflict, not class.
2co.author: Paul

gl.title: Freedom in Christ
gl.summary: In the churches of Galatia, someone demanded circumcision of Gentile converts. Paul refuses any mixed gospel. Justification by faith, fruit of the Spirit — does not mark the flesh. The freedom charter.
gl.author: Paul

ef.title: The church, the body of Christ
ef.summary: From prison in Rome, Paul describes the eternal plan: Jew and Gentile in one body. Ephesus lived the cult of Artemis; the letter falls to the ground — marriage, work, spiritual struggle. High doctrine, common life.
ef.author: Paul

fp.title: Joy in prison
fp.summary: Philippi, a Roman colony, was the first church in Europe. Paul writes in chains, calls for unity and quotes the hymn of Christ who emptied himself. Joy here does not wait for circumstances — it lives on Christ.
fp.author: Paul

cl.title: Christ is enough
cl.summary: In Colossae, someone was selling a gospel with visions, angels, and food rules. Paul responds from prison: in Christ all fullness dwells. There is no shortage of pieces in the Lord that the church has already received.
cl.author: Paul

1ts.title: A young church and the return of the Lord
1ts.summary: Paulo left quickly, pursued on Via Egnacia. Write to recent converts: the Lord will return, the dead in Christ will rise. Concrete consolation, not speculation about dates.
1ts.author: Paul

2ts.title: The day has not yet arrived
2ts.summary: Someone faked a letter from Paul and the church stopped working. 2 Thessalonians corrects the clock: there is apostasy before the end. In the meantime, stay and keep your hands busy.
2ts.author: Paul

1tm.title: How to take care of God's house
1tm.summary: Timothy pastors in Ephesus, a city of false teachers. Paul guides prayer, officers, widows and sound doctrine. The Gospel needs a well-cared for church — not just loose preaching.
1tm.author: Paul

2tm.title: Paul's testament
2tm.summary: Last letter, under Nero, close to death. Many abandoned him. Paul asks Timothy to come and preach the Word. A spiritual father delivers his testimony before leaving.
2tm.author: Paul

tt.title: Strong churches in Crete
tt.summary: Crete had a bad reputation; the churches were new. Titus must appoint presbyters and silence vain teachers. The grace that saves also educates. Faith that does not become conduct has not yet matured.
tt.author: Paul

fm.title: One slave, one master, the Gospel in the middle
fm.summary: Onesimus fled and found Paul in prison. The letter asks Philemon, in Colossae, to receive him as a brother. A sheet that shows the Gospel dismantling power relations within the Roman household.
fm.author: Paul

hb.title: Jesus is better - don't go back
hb.summary: Author unknown, before the fall of the temple in 70 A.D. Christians of Jewish origin, tired, looked back to the ancient cult. Hebrews shows the Son above angels, Moses and priests. The new covenant is fulfillment, not a plan B.
hb.author: Unknown

tg.title: Faith that is seen
tg.summary: Probably the oldest writing in the New Testament, from James, Jesus' brother, to the tribes in the diaspora. It confronts favoritism, loose tongue and faith without works. It does not contradict Paul: living faith produces fruit.
tg.author: James, brother of Jesus

1pe.title: Pilgrims under pressure
1pe.summary: Christians of Asia Minor, scattered and strange, suffer because of the name. The empire becomes hostile. Peter points out the incorruptible inheritance and example of Christ. Suffering well is testimony.
1pe.author: Pedro

2pe.title: Beware of false teachers
2pe.summary: Close to death, Peter warns: there will be those who mock the return of Christ. The Lord's delay is patience, not forgetfulness. Grow in grace — and don’t let yourselves be dragged down.
2pe.author: Pedro

1jo.title: Signs of life in Christ
1jo.summary: At the end of the century, some left the church denying that Christ came in the flesh. John offers simple tests: faith in the Son, love for brothers, practice of the truth. Communion with God is verified.
1jo.author: John the apostle

2jo.title: Truth, love and discernment
2jo.summary: Brief letter to a church: remain in the teaching of Christ. Itinerant missionaries are not always sane. Hospitality is a virtue; to receive those who deny the incarnation is to participate in the evil work.
2jo.author: John the apostle

3jo.title: Hospitality and pride in the church
3jo.summary: Gaius welcomes brothers; Diotrephes likes to be first and closes the door. 3 John honors those who serve in the rearguard and confront ego in the presbytery of a local church.
3jo.author: John the apostle

jd.title: I contended for faith
jd.summary: Judas, Jesus' brother, wanted to write about salvation and had to write a warning. Wicked men turn grace into debauchery. The letter is a cry to keep the deposit, without negotiating the Gospel.
jd.author: Judas, brother of Jesus

ap.title: The Lamb wins
ap.summary: John, exiled to Patmos at the end of the first century, writes to the seven churches of Asia under the cult of the emperor. Apocalypse is not a map of fear: it is hope for those who suffer. Behind Caesar's throne is another throne—and the Lamb reigns.
ap.author: John the apostle
